sentences.text: By this judgment this Tribunal shall decide the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 23.01.2023 at about 6.00 p.m, petitioner was riding bicycle from his college to his residence on left side of Madanayakanahalli- Thotadaguddadahalli road,
Kuderegere colony, near Farmhouse at that time a TATA Harrier XZA+20L Kryotec BSVI Model car bearing reg.No.T-1-222-PB-7753-F/KA-51-MT-8082 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner without following traffic (SCCH-12) 3 MVC. No.4562/2023 rules dashed to petitioner from behind and caused accident.
Petitioner sustained facial and head injury and other bodily injuries.
3. Immediately petitioner was shifted to Abhaya Vashist hospital for treatment and treated as inpatient from 23.01.2023 to 26.01.2023.
Petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
4. Petitioner was studying 1st yr. PUC in BGS College and he was meritorious student having bright future ahead of him.
He was hale and healthy prior to the accident.
Due tot he injuries sustained in the accident he is unable to attend the college to study and prevents him to study as before.
He is suffering from immense pain and suffering.
Respondent no.1 is the owner of vehicle, respondent no.2 is the GPA holder and respondent no.3 is the insurance company.
The Madanayakanahalli police have registered case under Sec.279, 337 of IPC in Crime no.53/2023.
The 1st respondent is the R.C owner, 2 nd respondent is the GPA holder and 3rd respondent is the insurance company.
All are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds, she prayed to allow the petition and award compensation.
5. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 to 3 are served.
2 nd respondent remained absent to the court.
Hence, he is placed ex-parte.
Respondent no.1 and 3 appeared before this court (SCCH-12) 4 MVC. No.4562/2023 through their respective counsel and filed written statement separately.
6. 1st respondent owner of car contended that, he is a doctor and was working at Pancham Manorog Hospital at Mohali, Punjab in the year 2023.

That during the time of loading the brand new Tata Harrier car to the transportation vehicle belonging to this respondent, driver employed by 2nd respondent caused an accident on 23.01.2023 damaging the car and injury to a passerby.
That FIR No.53/23 dt.23.01.2023 was registered by Madanayakanahally Police and 2nd respondent was aware of the same.
8. That 1st respondent approached Hon'ble Consumer Forum vide Consumer Complaint No.134/2023.

The Hon'ble Consumer Forum after perusing the documents and evidence produced by respondent no.1 herein was pleased to order a compensation of Rs.2,18,596/- to 1st respondent along with interest @ 9% p.a from the date of order till realization and the Hon'ble Consumer Forum had also directed the 2nd respondent to comply with the same within 45 days from the date of the order.
Despite order being sent to 2 nd respondent, it had failed to comply the same.
That at the time of accident the vehicle was in possession of 2 nd respondent and 1st respondent was in Mohali, Punjab and has nothing to do with the accident.
That 1st respondent has purchased a valid insurance which encompasses 3rd party liability.
That insurance is valid, it is the responsibility of 3 rd respondent to make good of the claim and 1st respondent is not liable in any manner to pay compensation to petitioner.

It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
The driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective D.L at the time of accident.
That insured has not complied Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act, concerned police have not complied Sec.158(6) of the said Act.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioner to prove negligence on part of the opponent vehicle driver got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.
He was minor when the petition was filed.
Then he attained the age of majority and guardian is discharged.
Petitioner himself appeared before the court to give evidence.
In his chief examination he reiterated petition averments.
He has produced FIR, first information, discharge summary, medical bills, I.D card and final report.

16. On perusal of those documents it can be seen that one Suresh Babu who is father of the petitioner has given first information to Madanayakanahalli Police station on the same day stating that, his son Kishore Naidu is studying in I PUC at BYS college.

That on 23.01.2023 while coming back from college at 6.00pm on Bicycle on the way near Kuduregere colony Farm house, one car bearing No. T-1-222-PB-7753-F dashed from (SCCH-12) 9 MVC. No.4562/2023 behind to his son.
That the accident he sustained injury to head and limbs.
That someone informed this first informant about the accident.
On the basis of this first information, Madanayakanahalli police have registered Crime No.53/2023 against the aforesaid car driver for the offence of negligence.

They have also filed final report against the car driver for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
17.
Wound certificate, spot mahazar, spot sketch are not produced by the petitioner side.
Respondents have also not produced those documents.
IMV notice and answer to IMV notice are produced by insurance company to show that driver fo the car had no D.L
In the answer to IMV notice there is no mention about the D.L number fo the driver and its validity period.
No documents are produced regarding negligence of petitioner and no negligence on part of opponent car driver in the evidence of respondent no.1 and 3.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 also nothing proving the negligence on part of petitioner is established.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court the negligence on part of opponent car driver is established.
Accordingly, this issue is answered In the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :
To prove his age petitioner has produced aadhaar card at Ex.P.6 which shows his date of birth as 07.03.2006.
Accident took place on 23.01.2023.
She was aged 16 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 16 years at the time of accident.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was a student studying in BGS college.
No documents are produced to show his education, but in cross of P.w.1, petitioner admitted that after the accident he continued the education and he was not failed in the class.

Therefore, there is no avocation, earning income to the petitioner but, even in the case of accident to minor, compensation has to be worked out in non pecuniary heads, including treatment, transportation, attendant charges, pain and suffering and loss of amenities of life.

The petitioner being non earning member,

Accordingly, the quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained head injury, facial injuries i.e, fracture of anterior aspect of bony nasal septum with adjacent hematoma, soft tissue swelling in frontal region of scalp with extension to root of nose and preseptal compartment of right orbit, fracture of alveolar process of maxilla with uprooting of right central incisor, soft tissue swelling in left parieto temporal region of scalp swelling (SCCH-12) 11 MVC. swelling in frontal region of scalp reaching up to root of nose and other bodily injuries.
The said injuries are grievous in nature.
The records show that he underwent surgery.
He was in hospital from 23.01.2033 to 26.01.2023 i.e for 04 days asper Ex.P.3 discharge summary of Abhay Vasishtha hospital.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .
(ii) For Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P4 and 7.
They show that he has spent Rs.75,451/- + Rs.24,320/- for medical expenses.
Those bills are disputed by the respondents, but nothing worthwhile is brought out to disbelieve the bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.99,771/- .
(iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was in hospital for 04 days.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.2,000/- is awarded.
(iv) For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 04 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence attendant charges of Rs.2,000/-is awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period: As there is no income can be considered for minor, no compensation is awarded for loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges: It is stated that petitioner was shifted from spot of accident to the hospital.
He spent money for (SCCH-12) 12 MVC. No.4562/2023 traveling to hospital.
Considering those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.3,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.

In his evidence he has produced vehicle purchase bill, delivery of vehicle photographs, registration form, bill raised with 2 nd respondent Cargo company for the transport of the vehicle raised on 22.01.2023, payment (SCCH-12) 14 MVC.
No.4562/2023 receipt of Rs.20,000/- paid to 2nd respondent for transportation of vehicle, order sheet in consumer complaint No.134/2023 which is filed by 1st respondent against 2nd respondent manager of cargo company along with judgment in consumer complaint which shows 1st respondent was awarded with compensation of Rs.2,18,596/- from 2nd respondent for the loss, mental agony,
repair charges of the car etc.
22.
1st respondent contended that even after such award, 2 nd respondent has not paid the amount to 1 st respondent.
2nd respondent is party before this court and he remained absent and has not contested the case.
Therefore, all those averments made by 1st respondent against 2nd respondent are uncontested and unchallenged.

There is evidence on record to prove that, 2 nd respondent cargo company's car driver was negligent in the accident and the owner of car has filed consumer case against the cargo company and awarded with compensation.
These facts are not in dispute.
Therefore, the question would be whether pay and recovery has to be ordered and if yes, whether recovery has to be made from the owner or from the cargo company.

23. The 1st respondent relied upon the judgment in Manager, Bajaj General Ins. Company V/s Bheem Raj and another, ILR 2015 KAR 4759 in which the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has relied upon the judgment in United India Insurance Company Ltd V/s Lehru and others (2003) 3 SCC, 338, in which it is held that the breach must be on part of insured.

sentences.text: An (SCCH-12) 15 MVC.

No.4562/2023 example is given in the said case stating that if the vehicle is driven by the thief and if it is caught and ascertained that the said thief had no licence, can the insurance company disown liability.
It is held that the answer is emphatic NO.
It is further held that insurance company must establish that the breach was on part of the insured.
24. Considering all these facts it can be noticed that driver of 2nd respondent has not produced D.L before police or before this court.

Therefore, in the opinion of this court since there is valid insurance policy existing on the date of accident, insurance company is liable to pay compensation and entitled to recover it from 2nd respondent cargo company who was possessor of the vehicle at the time of accident and entrusted the same to the person having no D.L.
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,10,000/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.
